images.title: Raghav's two wall clocks
images.purpose: Put Raghav's two wall clocks in front of the student before any time is said: the clock before his yoga and the clock after it, with only hands and no digits.
images.composition: Two analogue clocks side by side, each above its own yoga mat, with the captions Before yoga and After yoga under the mats, on one plain white frame.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Exactly two analogue wall clocks, side by side, the same size. Each clock is a circle 360 px across, with a dark teal #0B3C49 rim 14 px thick and a pale face #E8F4F8 inside it. LEFT CLOCK: centre at x 400, y 330 (the circle spans x 220 to 580 and y 150 to 510). RIGHT CLOCK: centre at x 1056, y 330 (the circle spans x 876 to 1236 and y 150 to 510). On each clock: 60 small tick marks around the face in dark #2B2B2B, of which 12 are long (4 px wide, from radius 146 to 162 px, at the 12 numbers) and 48 are short (2 px wide, from radius 154 to 162 px); the 12 numbers 1 to 12 in dark #1F2937 sans-serif bold (32 px), centred on a ring of radius 126 px from the centre, 12 at the top, 3 on the right, 6 at the bottom, 9 on the left; a small dark #2B2B2B centre dot 14 px across; exactly two hands, a long minute hand and a short hour hand, and no seconds hand. The minute hand is amber #E69F00, 106 px long and 8 px wide with a round end, so its tip stops just inside the ring of numbers. The hour hand is teal blue #0072B2, 70 px long and 12 px wide with a round end. Angles are measured clockwise from 12. LEFT CLOCK: the minute hand points at the number 7 (210 degrees, its tip at x 347, y 422); the hour hand points between 5 and 6, closer to 6 than to 5 (167.5 degrees, its tip at x 415, y 398). RIGHT CLOCK: the minute hand points at the number 11 (330 degrees, its tip at x 1003, y 238); the hour hand points just before 6, almost on the 6 (177.5 degrees, its tip at x 1059, y 400). Under each clock lies one yoga mat, a flat rounded rectangle 400 px wide and 60 px high (corner radius 10 px), filled green #009E73 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline: the left mat spans x 200 to 600 and y 580 to 640, the right mat spans x 856 to 1256 and y 580 to 640. Under the left mat, centred at x 400 and y 705, the caption Before yoga; under the right mat, centred at x 1056 and y 705, the caption After yoga, both in dark #1F2937 sans-serif bold (44 px). No digital time, no time written as digits with a colon, no person, no seconds hand and no other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any time written as digits with a colon, any digital clock, any answer or number of minutes written anywhere in the frame

a seconds hand, a third clock, a person, or hands in any other positions than the ones given: the left clock minute hand on 7 and hour hand between 5 and 6, the right clock minute hand on 11 and hour hand just before 6
images.takeaway: The two clocks show different times, so some time went by between them while Raghav did his yoga.
images.description: Two wall clocks above two yoga mats, captioned Before yoga and After yoga, with the hands in different places on each clock and no times written.
images.context: Concept image for the hook, Raghav's Morning Yoga. It follows the idea of the opener in your maths book (two wall clocks, one before and one after Raghav's yoga, with only hands and no digits) and gives no time and no answer.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student look at where the hands are on each clock, but do not say a time or a number of minutes on this picture. The slip to watch: reading the minute hand on 7 as 7 minutes.

image_decisions.why: The two wall clocks, with only hands and no times written, put the hook question, how much time went by, in front of the student without giving the answer.
